transport: AWS CLI 2.36.28 via scripts/aws/aws_cli.py; signed raw AWS JSON via scripts/aws/signed_requests.py; temporary SigV4 GET adaptation for S3 raw XML; debug request body and response-only extraction; signing logs discarded
scope: One uniquely owned bucket name, created and absence-verified deleted in three sequential lifecycles as followup evidence was requested; 18 uniquely named non-organization single-region trail attempts, six successful. No StartLogging, no changes to existing resources or logging configuration. LookupEvents only retains events correlated to the owned target requests.
redactions: Account ID consistently replaced by 111111111111; credential identifiers omitted; source IP replaced by documentation address; owned resource names and native request/event IDs retained. Unrelated LookupEvents rows and all pagination tokens discarded.

principal_type.scope: CreateTrail S3 permission preflight, independently varying only the GetBucketAcl or PutObject statement while the other statement remains an otherwise-correct unconditional service-principal grant scoped to that exact owned trail SourceArn and SourceAccount.
principal_type.presence: Null=false succeeds and Null=true fails independently at both permission gates.
principal_type.controls: No-PrincipalType baseline before and after the initial literal matrix succeeds. Every bucket-policy update succeeds. All six successful trails report IsLogging=false.
principal_type.limitation: This proves the observed preflight condition value, not the aws:PrincipalType value of later asynchronous log delivery, which was intentionally never enabled. It does not identify the internal role ARN or imply the CloudTrail audit userIdentity.type field must equal the policy context value.

marker_effects.ordering: Each case records an empty case-specific prefix before CreateTrail, its native result, then ListObjectsV2 and HeadObject. All successful creates and all six ACL-gate failures leave a zero-byte marker. The six PutObject-gate failures leave no marker. Markers remain after trail deletion until explicitly deleted.
marker_effects.limitation: This is externally observed side-effect ordering around CreateTrail, not a trace of the internal order or concurrency of S3 permission calls. No S3 PutObject was issued by the probe to create these markers.

lookup_timestamp_projection.correlation: The first bounded event-history poll returns exactly the two owned requests. CLI event matches the captured native response request ID; raw event matches the exact nonexistent unique ResourceName and timestamp parameters.
lookup_timestamp_projection.limitation: The shared raw POST helper exposes status/body but not request-ID headers. Raw correlation therefore uses the unique resource name rather than an independently captured response ID. The observed event projection drops fractional seconds; this does not prove how subsecond event filtering is internally evaluated.

s3_encoding.observation: Raw signed GET /?encoding-type=url&list-type=2 returns EncodingType=url with literal slash characters in marker Key values. Both explicit-EncodingType and omitted-EncodingType AWS CLI observations also return literal slashes.
s3_encoding.limitation: The raw GET proves slash preservation is native XML behavior, not only client-side decoding. This capture does not test other special characters. Its Prefix is empty; raw nonempty Prefix encoding was not exercised.

conclusions.ownership_and_cleanup: Exact designated-account identity was verified before each lifecycle. Only the uniquely named bucket and uniquely named trail attempts in this fixture were mutated. All 18 trail names return TrailNotFoundException after their attempt/deletion; all three bucket lifecycles end with KeyCount=0, successful DeleteBucket and HeadBucket HTTP 404. Owned marker objects were individually deleted. No unrelated audit-event payload was retained.

observations.label: owned-lookup-timestamp-raw
observations.limitation: Shared signed_requests helper returns status/body but not response request-ID headers; correlate this event by exact unique ResourceName plus timestamp parameters.
